facts.text: Searsport was named after David Sears of Boston, who funded its founding.
Settled in the 1760s, Searsport became an incorporated town on February 13, 1845, carved from Prospect and Belfast.
In the 19th century, Searsport’s 17 shipyards built 200 vessels, supplying a tenth of the U.S. deep‑water merchant captains per square mile.
The Penobscot Marine Museum spans a campus of historic sea‑captain homes, showcasing maritime art, ship models, and navigation tools.

Searsport ranks Maine’s second‑largest deep‑water port and served as the Penobscot Bay terminus for the Northern Seaport Railroad, which shipped timber, potatoes, and coal without Maine Central rates.
Searsport harbor offers a sheltered anchorage about 2 by 3 miles, with a mean low‑water depth of 40 feet and a tidal swing of 10 feet.
